## Problem

**Given the radar scans observed so far, will a tornado appear in the next 5 and 10 minutes
when none is visible yet?**

The framing matters: a tornado already on the radar can be carried forward by any detector.
The useful question is the one before that, so the evaluation is built to exclude detection.

### The target, scan by scan

A TorNet sample is four scans of one storm about five minutes apart, each with its own tornado
label. The model sees the two oldest scans and answers for each of the two newest.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph input["input: 2 scans"]
        s1["t−15 min<br/>label 0"]
        s2["t−10 min<br/>label 0"]
    end
    subgraph target["targets: 2 scans"]
        s3["t−5 min<br/>label ?"]
        s4["t<br/>label ?"]
    end
    s1 --> s2 --> s3 --> s4
    s1 --> model(("model"))
    s2 --> model
    model -. "P(tornado at t−5)" .-> s3
    model -. "P(tornado at t)" .-> s4
```

The four labels read as a pattern, and only some patterns are the question:

| pattern | meaning | role |
|---|---|---|
| `0001`, `0011` | no tornado in the inputs, one in the last target | **pre-onset case**: the positives |
| `0111`, `1111`, … | a tornado already visible in an input scan | *ongoing*: excluded from the positives |
| `0000` | no tornado | negatives; every null sample is kept |

### How a prediction is scored

Each test sample gets a probability per horizon. Three views of the negatives, following the
TorNet paper:

| view | negatives | measures |
|---|---|---|
| NC | all nulls | overall skill |
| RC | random non-tornadic storms | tornado vs ordinary storm |
| **WC** | tornado-**warned** storms with no tornado | **the hard case; the headline number** |

The metric is AUC (and AUCPR) with bootstrap intervals, plus the best-CSI threshold.

The frozen published TorNet detector supplies two reference points on the same samples:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    floor["<b>floor</b><br/>judge on the newest observed scan<br/><i>assume the future looks like the present</i>"]
    head["<b>the model</b><br/>P(tornado at +h) from the two observed scans"]
    ceil["<b>ceiling</b><br/>judge on the real future scan<br/><i>a perfect forecast</i>"]
    floor --> head --> ceil
```

A result is the model's AUC against the floor as a **paired bootstrap difference on the same
files** with its 95% interval. The gap from floor to ceiling is the whole prize for forecasting
radar: about 0.05 to 0.07 WC AUC on one year.

### Power

Pre-onset positives are rare by construction, roughly 200 to 275 per test year, so every
pre-onset number carries about ±0.025 AUC and differences under about 0.03 are not resolvable
on one year. Every comparison is therefore paired with its interval stated, and only more seeds
and more years shrink the noise.

## Data

TorNet v1.1 (MIT Lincoln Laboratory; Veillette et al., AIES 2024; CC BY 4.0), on the Hugging
Face Hub as **`jakeryderv/tornet`**: every sample, every field, as Parquet.

### A sample

One storm, four NEXRAD WSR-88D scans, on a polar grid centred on the storm: 120 azimuths ×
240 range gates (250 m) × 2 elevation tilts (0.5°, 0.9°).

| field | shape / type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DBZ`, `VEL`, `KDP`, `RHOHV`, `ZDR`, `WIDTH` | (4, 120, 240, 2) float16 | reflectivity (dBZ), radial velocity (m/s), specific differential phase (°/km), correlation coefficient, differential reflectivity (dB), spectrum width (m/s) |
| `range_folded_mask` | (4, 120, 240, 2) uint8 | 1 where `VEL` / `WIDTH` are range-folded |
| `frame_labels` | int8[4] | tornado present in each scan |
| `time` | int64[4] | each scan's time, Unix seconds |
| `category` | string | `TOR` confirmed, `WRN` warned but none, `NUL` random storm |
| `ef_number` | int8 | EF rating for `TOR`, −1 otherwise |
| `az_lower`, `az_upper`, `rng_lower`, `rng_upper` | float32 | the chip's azimuth (°) and range (m) limits |
| `tornado_start_time`, `tornado_end_time` | int64 | the tornado's interval, 0 when none |
| `event_id`, `episode_id`, `site`, `lat`, `lon`, `filename` | | metadata |

Empty gates are NaN; values are physical units.

### How much

| year | train | test | | year | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2013 | 3,498 | 573 | | 2018 | 15,360 | 2,518 |
| 2014 | 17,447 | 2,546 | | 2019 | 20,588 | 4,031 |
| 2015 | 19,721 | 3,902 | | 2020 | 18,147 | 4,756 |
| 2016 | 18,791 | 2,951 | | 2021 | 19,051 | 4,268 |
| 2017 | 16,927 | 3,145 | | 2022 | 22,136 | 2,777 |

203,133 samples: 171,666 train, 31,467 test; 13,857 `TOR`, 64,510 `WRN`, 124,766 `NUL`.

### From a row to tensors

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    raw["6 products<br/>(4, 120, 240, 2)<br/>physical units, NaN"] --> norm["normalise per product<br/>(x − mid) / half-range<br/>NaN → −3"]
    norm --> cat["12 radar channels"]
    mask["range-folded mask"] --> cat2["+ 2 = 14 channels"]
    cat --> cat2
    limits["azimuth & range limits"] --> coords["CoordConv coordinates<br/>(2, 120, 240): range, 1/range"]
    cat2 --> x["x: (scans, 14, 120, 240)"]
```

The normalisation is the published detector's (DBZ −20…60, VEL −60…60, KDP −2…5,
RHOHV 0.2…1.04, ZDR −1…8, WIDTH 0…9), so its weights apply unchanged. Each item also carries
the per-scan labels, the real lead in minutes of each target from the last input, the input
spacing, and the authors' sample weight (EF2+ ×2, warned storms ×0.5).

## Splits and setup

**Partitions.** The authors' `train` and `test` splits, per year. The first slice uses
**2015 only**: 19,721 training and 3,902 test samples, 275 pre-onset cases in the test set.

**Validation** is held out from the training partition by **whole days** (15% of days, 32 of
212 in 2015), never by random sample: consecutive samples of one storm are near duplicates
and would leak. Checkpoints are selected and training stopped on this split.

**Loading.** Shards of the configured years are fetched into the Hub file cache once (2015 is
about 12 GB) and streamed with pyarrow one shard at a time (256 samples each); shard order is
reshuffled every epoch and rows within a shard are shuffled; DataLoader workers take disjoint
shards. No uncompressed copy of the dataset is written.

**Weights.** The published detector, converted once from its Keras checkpoint to a torch state
dict and published as `jakeryderv/tornet-detector-torch` (MIT, as the original; verified to
2e-5 in the logits). Nothing is downloaded by hand: `uv sync`, then `onset-train <config>`.

**A run** writes `params.json`, `history.csv`, `checkpoints/{best,last}.pt`, `scores/` (per-view
prediction CSVs with the label pattern and pre-onset flags, `summary.json`, likelihood maps,
`features.npz`) and `results.json`. `onset-summary` tabulates finished runs; `onset-score`
rescores any checkpoint.

## Modeling

The published TorNet detector, fine-tuned on the onset target, with the authors' head on top.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    s1["scan t−15<br/>14 × 120 × 240"] --> enc1["TorNet encoder<br/>(shared, fine-tuned)"]
    s2["scan t−10<br/>14 × 120 × 240"] --> enc2["TorNet encoder<br/>(shared, fine-tuned)"]
    enc1 --> f1["384 × 8 × 15"]
    enc2 --> f2["384 × 8 × 15"]
    f1 --> comb{"combiner"}
    f2 --> comb
    comb --> head["head: 1×1 conv 512 → 1×1 conv 256 → 1×1 conv<br/>per-cell logit map, max over cells"]
    head --> p5["P(tornado at +5)"]
    head --> p10["P(tornado at +10)"]
```

### Encoder

The TorNet CNN: four blocks of CoordConv 3×3 layers (2, 2, 3, 3 layers; 48, 96, 192, 384
filters), each block followed by 2×2 max pooling and dropout 0.1, ending in a 384 × 8 × 15 map.
A CoordConv layer concatenates the two coordinate channels before its convolution. Initialised
from the published weights; trained at a tenth of the head's learning rate.

### Combiner

| `combiner` | what the head sees | head |
|---|---|---|
| `concat` (default) | the two maps side by side, 768 × 8 × 15 | fresh, 2 output maps |
| `extrapolate` | per horizon, f(+h) = f_new + (lead_h / Δt) · (f_new − f_old), real scan times | one shared 384-channel head, optionally the published head's weights |

With two scans a feature's history is a line. `concat` lets the head learn any combination of
value and slope; `extrapolate` fixes the slope rule and the clock. Same expressive power,
different inductive bias.

### Head and loss

The authors' head: 1×1 convolutions 512 and 256 with ReLU, a 1×1 convolution to one logit per
cell, the maximum over the 8 × 15 cells. The map before the max is the spatial likelihood map.
4.9M parameters in total.

| | |
|---|---|
| loss | weighted binary cross-entropy per horizon; sample weights EF2+ ×2, warned ×0.5 |
| optional | `consistency_weight`: L1 between f(+h) and the encoder's features of the real scan at +h (detached); `extrapolate` only |
| optimiser | AdamW, lr 1e-4 head / 1e-5 encoder, weight decay 1e-4, gradient clip 1.0 |
| schedule | cosine over the epoch cap (8); early stopping on validation head AUC, patience 2 |
| precision, batch | mixed precision; batch 16 |

### The judge

The frozen published detector reads the newest observed scan (floor) and the real future scan
(ceiling) for every test sample and horizon. It never trains.

## Baseline and experiments

All numbers: 2015 test partition, 3,902 samples, 275 pre-onset cases; pre-onset cases vs
warned storms (WC AUC); paired bootstrap against the floor in brackets.

### Baseline (2026-10-14)

Two versions were compared. The first carried a U-Net decoder drawing the future velocity and
reflectivity, trained by a heat-map-weighted L1 and the judge's cross-entropy on the drawn chip,
as an auxiliary signal for the shared encoder (10.1M parameters). The second is the model
above, encoder and head only (4.9M).

| horizon | floor | ceiling | decoder + judge losses | **encoder + head** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| +5 min | 0.709 | 0.764 | 0.716 (+0.007 [−0.030, +0.040]) | **0.739** (+0.030 [−0.006, +0.064]) |
| +10 min | 0.722 | 0.796 | 0.729 (+0.007 [−0.015, +0.031]) | **0.735** (+0.013 [−0.011, +0.038]) |

Head-only minus the decoder model on the same files: +0.023 [+0.004, +0.043] at +5 min,
+0.006 [−0.010, +0.021] at +10. The decoder was dropped. Both runs overfit after epoch 2 to 3
on one year of training data, which early stopping now addresses.

Reading: the fine-tuned model beats the published detector on the newest scan by a small
margin whose interval touches zero, and the ceiling stays 0.055 to 0.074 above the floor. The
information for "a tornado in ten minutes" is mostly not in two radar chips.

### Experiments

| run | question | status |
|---|---|---|
| `y2015`, seed 1234 | does the Hub loader reproduce 0.739 / 0.735 | running 2026-10-15 |
| `y2015`, seed 2 | seed spread | running |
| `y2015_extrapolate` | does the explicit trend rule with the real clock help | running |
| `y2015_extrapolate_consistency` | does a feature-space consistency loss help | running |
| `y2015`, `encoder_lr_scale` 0.03 | gentler fine-tuning against overfitting | planned |
| `y2015`, `encoder_trainable` false | the frozen-encoder control | planned |

Results land here as they finish, from `onset-summary`.

### Next

More years from the Hub, which addresses both the overfitting and the power limit; then
environmental fields joined on `features.npz`, and longer scan histories, where a recurrent
combiner would earn its place.
